## How do I add or change an account (category)?

<a id="chart-of-accounts"></a>

The Chart of Accounts is the list of categories your money is sorted into: bank accounts, income, expenses, what you own and owe.

**Where:** **Accounting › Chart of Accounts** (`/accounts`)

1. Open the Chart of Accounts (Ctrl+A) and click "Add Account". → **Accounting › Chart of Accounts** (`/accounts`)
2. Choose the type and detail type, give it a name, and pick a tax line if your accountant uses one. Save.
3. An account you no longer use: make it inactive instead of deleting it, so its history stays.

> Good to know: Any account picker also offers "Set Up" for a name it does not know, so you can add the account without leaving the form.

*In the app: Help & Glossary → "How do I add or change an account (category)?", or ask Ask AI.*

## How do I make a journal entry?

<a id="journal-entry"></a>

A journal entry moves amounts between accounts directly. It is mostly used by accountants for adjustments. Debits must equal credits.

**Where:** **Accounting › Journal entries** (`/journal?new=1`)

1. Open Journal entries and click "New Journal Entry". → **Accounting › Journal entries** (`/journal?new=1`)
2. Add a line for each account with a debit or a credit. A line on Accounts Receivable needs the customer in the Name column; a line on Accounts Payable needs the vendor.
3. Save. The form will not save until debits equal credits.

> Good to know: Not an accountant? Most things have their own screen (invoice, bill, check, transfer). Use those first.
>
> Good to know: Ask AI can draft a journal entry for you to approve: ask it to "record…" and review the proposed entry.

*In the app: Help & Glossary → "How do I make a journal entry?", or ask Ask AI.*

## How do I close the month?

<a id="close-month"></a>

Close the month is a guided checklist: reconcile, tidy up, review balances, then lock the books with a closing date and download a report pack.

**Where:** **Admin › Close the month** (`/month-end`)

1. Open Close the month and pick the "Month to close". → **Admin › Close the month** (`/month-end`)
2. Work through each step. Use "Mark as reviewed", or "Skip this step…" with a reason.
3. Click "Close the books" and set the closing date password. Transactions dated on or before the closing date can then be changed only with that password.
4. Click "Download report pack (PDF)".

> Good to know: The closing date can also be set on its own in Preferences ("Set Closing Date").

*In the app: Help & Glossary → "How do I close the month?", or ask Ask AI.*

## How do I close the year?

<a id="close-year"></a>

Year-End Close moves the year’s net income into Retained Earnings with one closing entry.

**Where:** **Accounting › Year-End Close** (`/year-end`)

1. Finish and close the last month of the year first. → **Admin › Close the month** (`/month-end`)
2. Open Year-End Close, enter the Fiscal Year and confirm. → **Accounting › Year-End Close** (`/year-end`)
3. To reverse it, void the closing entry it created.

> Good to know: Reports work without this step: they show prior-year profit as Retained Earnings on their own. Ask your accountant whether they want the closing entry.

*In the app: Help & Glossary → "How do I close the year?", or ask Ask AI.*

## How do I send my books to my accountant?

<a id="accountants-copy"></a>

Send the whole file, a ledger export, or an Accountant’s Copy that lets your accountant fix an earlier period while you keep working.

**Where:** **Admin › Accountant's Copy** (`/accountant/accountants-copy`)

1. A copy of everything: File > Save Copy As…, or File > Create Portable Company File… for a smaller file to email. → **Setup › Company File** (`/company-file`)
2. Just the numbers: File > Export Shareable Ledger, as an Excel Workbook or a PDF Summary.
3. Both working at once: open Accountant’s Copy, pick the dividing date and create the copy. When the changes file comes back, open it there, check each change, then import. → **Admin › Accountant's Copy** (`/accountant/accountants-copy`)

> Good to know: For an auditor who should see only one period, use Period Copy.

*In the app: Help & Glossary → "How do I send my books to my accountant?", or ask Ask AI.*

## How do I track income and expenses by department, location or class?

<a id="classes-tracking"></a>

Classes & locations lets you tag each transaction line, then report profit for each tag.

**Where:** **Accounting › Classes & locations** (`/tracking`)

1. Open Classes & locations and click "Add Class" (or "Add Location") for each one. → **Accounting › Classes & locations** (`/tracking`)
2. Pick the class on the lines of invoices, bills, checks and journal entries.
3. Run Profit & Loss by class. → **Reports › Profit & Loss by class** (`/reports/pl-by-class`)

*In the app: Help & Glossary → "How do I track income and expenses by department, location or class?", or ask Ask AI.*

## How do I make a budget or forecast?

<a id="budgets"></a>

Budgets holds a target (or a forecast) by account and month, and compares it with what actually happened.

**Where:** **Budgets** (`/budgets`)

1. Open Budgets and click "New Budget". Give it a name and fiscal year and choose what you are planning. → **Budgets** (`/budgets`)
2. Type the monthly amounts, or use "Create from actuals" to start from a past year.
3. Open the budget to see Actual, Budget and Variance side by side.

*In the app: Help & Glossary → "How do I make a budget or forecast?", or ask Ask AI.*

## How do I make a transaction repeat (rent, subscriptions)?

<a id="recurring-transactions"></a>

Recurring transactions saves a transaction you enter again and again, so it repeats on a schedule or with one click.

**Where:** **Accounting › Recurring transactions** (`/recurring`)

1. Enter the transaction once, then save it as recurring from its form (Ctrl+M memorizes it).
2. Open Recurring transactions and set how often it repeats. → **Accounting › Recurring transactions** (`/recurring`)

*In the app: Help & Glossary → "How do I make a transaction repeat (rent, subscriptions)?", or ask Ask AI.*

## How do I see who changed or deleted something?

<a id="audit-trail"></a>

The Audit Trail records every change: who made it, when, and the values before and after. It cannot be switched off.

**Where:** **Admin › Audit Trail** (`/audit-trail`)

1. Open the Audit Trail and filter by Action, Entity Type and dates. Click a line to see the values before and after. → **Admin › Audit Trail** (`/audit-trail`)
2. For voided and deleted transactions only, open the Voided/Deleted Transactions report. → **Voided/Deleted Transactions** (`/reports/voided-deleted`)

*In the app: Help & Glossary → "How do I see who changed or deleted something?", or ask Ask AI.*

## How do I track equipment and depreciation?

<a id="fixed-assets"></a>

Fixed Assets lists the equipment, vehicles and other things the business owns for more than a year, with their cost, and posts straight-line depreciation for you.

**Where:** **Operations › Fixed Assets** (`/fixed-assets`)

1. Open Fixed Assets and click "Add Asset". Enter the Asset Name, Cost, Salvage Value, Useful Life (months) and the Placed in Service date. → **Operations › Fixed Assets** (`/fixed-assets`)
2. Each period, click Depreciate on the asset, check the Monthly Amount and the Depreciation Date, then "Post Depreciation".
3. Schedule shows every period and which ones are posted.

> Good to know: Depreciation here is straight-line: (Cost - Salvage) / Useful Life per month. For another method, post the journal entry your accountant gives you.

*In the app: Help & Glossary → "How do I track equipment and depreciation?", or ask Ask AI.*
